setup_name: ADR vs home-market earnings dislocation (cross-border arb)
instrument: US-listed ADRs of Japanese stocks vs Tokyo shares, USD/JPY hedge
time_of_day: US session after a Tokyo-close news event; exit at Tokyo open
universe_filter: ~50 dual-listed Japanese names (e.g. Sony, Honda, NTT); company reports or news after the Tokyo close
conditions: Company releases earnings/news after Tokyo close
ADR in New York moves X% vs Tokyo close (FX-adjusted)
Trader judges the NY reaction too small or too large given the news and past earnings reactions
entry_trigger: Buy (or short) the ADR in New York when its move looks mispriced versus how Tokyo will open; hedge the yen exposure
stop: None mechanical; risk is the Tokyo open gap (limit-up/limit-down can trap the position)
target_or_exit: Unwind against the Tokyo shares at the Tokyo open
management: Often run delta neutral (long one name, short another) so FX legs net out
stated_edge: Algorithms price ADRs well on quiet days off Nikkei futures, S&P futures and USD/JPY, but misprice earnings and high-volatility events; a specialist who reads the numbers judges the reaction better
data_needed: Foreign-market prices, ADR ratios, FX, news/earnings text, ability to collapse cross-border trades
mcf_translation: Not mappable to MCF's US 5-min bar lab. Closest analog: US stocks that reprice on overnight news vs futures-implied open (gap fade/extension study).

setup_name: Crisis-day beta pair: short high-beta, long defensive
universe_filter: Pairs of names in the same market, one high-beta (e.g. auto maker) and one defensive (e.g. telecom), both down similar amounts
conditions: Index futures down sharply (about 3%)
High-beta and low-beta names show similar % drops in the US session
entry_trigger: Short the high-beta name, buy the defensive name in equal dollar amounts
target_or_exit: Close when the home market opens and the beta gap re-asserts
stated_edge: During forced liquidation, prices move in lockstep; on the next open the high-beta name falls far more than the defensive one
stated_stats: One cited example: high-beta name fell ~15% vs ~2% for the defensive name
data_needed: Beta estimates (computable from daily bars); historical crisis days are few
mcf_translation: On days SPY gap/close down > 2.5%, find pairs within a sector where daily-bar beta differs a lot but same-day returns are within 1%; long low-beta / short high-beta at close, exit next close; measure spread return.

setup_name: Absorption fade at a price that buyers/sellers cannot get through
instrument: futures (10-yr note, 5-yr note, T-bond, ultra bond; also ES)
time_of_day: first 2-3 hours after the open; more trades on high-news days (e.g. payrolls)
universe_filter: Deep, liquid futures order books; avoid thin books (crude, gold, DAX) for discretionary scalping
conditions: Market grinds toward a price level
Repeated hits at the level fail to trade through; large traded volume at the level without price progress
Fresh resting size reloads at the level
entry_trigger: Join the side that is holding the level (e.g. short against the level that buyers cannot lift), placing a limit order where possible
stop: 1-2 ticks beyond the level for a fade; if price is 2 ticks against and new sellers do not quickly push it back to entry, exit; emergency stop-market 3-5 ticks away
target_or_exit: 2-6 ticks typical; exit manually when order flow shows the move stalling rather than relying on a trailing stop
management: All-in/all-out sizing; re-enter if exited too early; scratch at break-even if no follow-through; hold 2-12 min typically
stated_edge: Prices move only when market orders overwhelm resting liquidity; watching traded volume at each price shows where real interest defends a level
stated_stats: 3-10 trades on a typical day, up to ~20-25 on volatile days; targets shrank from 12-14 to 4-7 ticks after HFT
data_needed: Level 2 / depth of market, tick-level trades with aggressor side, futures data
mcf_translation: Crude proxy only: on 5-min bars, a level touched 3+ times with high volume and no close beyond it -> fade with stop just beyond the level. Real signal needs order book.

setup_name: Inside-market size imbalance: lean with the heavy side
conditions: Inside bid size far exceeds inside offer size (e.g. ~10:1) or vice versa
Aggressive market orders are sweeping successive levels on one side
entry_trigger: If wanting to sell when the bid is much larger, rest a sell limit on the thin offer (likely to fill); if buying in that case, take the offer with a market order. When market orders wipe out several bid levels, go with the sellers or stand aside
target_or_exit: A few ticks, until the book evens out
management: Scratch trades that do not move quickly
stated_edge: Heavy one-sided interest tends to keep trades printing on the thin side until the book rebalances

universe_filter: SPY (or other ETFs classified as mean-reverting on the daily interval)
conditions: 2-period RSI on daily closes falls below 30
stop: None (guest argues stops cut mean-reversion trades before they revert)
management: Fixed ~15% of account per position across ~7 algos; no leverage
stated_edge: SPY has shown daily mean reversion since roughly the 1980s-90s (earlier it showed momentum); oversold dips tend to bounce
stated_stats: Guest recalls Sharpe above 1 over 10-15 years and smaller 2008 drawdown than buy-and-hold (not precise)
mcf_translation: Daily bars: RSI(2) on SPY close; long at close when RSI2<30, exit at close when RSI2>70; also test 5-min version on liquid ETFs as an intraday analog (RSI(2) on 5-min closes, flat by close).

setup_name: RSI momentum (buy overbought, sell oversold) on momentum-regime assets
instrument: ETFs/ETNs (GDXJ intraday, HYG 2-hour, inverse-vol ETNs XIV/SVXY)
universe_filter: Assets the regime scan classifies as momentum-persistent on that bar interval
conditions: Asset/interval classified as momentum (see regime-scan setup)
RSI moves into overbought zone
entry_trigger: Buy when RSI crosses into overbought (exact mirror of mean-reversion rule); short GDXJ when RSI goes oversold
stop: Indicator-based exit; fixed stops/targets only on weaker-anomaly assets
target_or_exit: Exit when RSI drops to oversold (or opposite threshold)
management: 15% of account per trade, ~4-5 assets at a time
stated_edge: Some assets show persistent trend behaviour at specific bar intervals; using a momentum rule on them and avoiding them for mean reversion
stated_stats: Combined 7-algo backtest claims 60-70%/yr; live ~17% YTD with Sharpe ~2 over ~15 months (heavily driven by inverse-vol products)
mcf_translation: For each ETF in MCF universe and each bar size (5-min, 30-min, 60-min aggregated, daily), compute returns of RSI(n) momentum rule vs mean-reversion rule; trade the rule that wins in the trailing window. Intraday: RSI(14) on 5-min > 70 -> long, exit < 30, flat at close.

setup_name: Quarterly momentum vs mean-reversion regime scan ('binocular')
time_of_day: run quarterly across 30-min, 1-hour, 2-hour, daily, weekly intervals
universe_filter: All ETFs; ~95% classify as random walk and are skipped
conditions: For each asset x bar interval, measure expected return of an oscillator-based momentum rule (x-axis) and mean-reversion rule (y-axis)
Classify into momentum, mean-reversion or random-walk quadrant
Pick 4-5 assets with the strongest anomaly / best risk-reward
entry_trigger: Selection only; trades come from simple 2-5 parameter rules matched to the regime
management: Few parameters (<10, usually 5-6) to limit overfitting
stated_edge: The edge is in choosing the asset/timeframe, not the entry rule; most assets are efficient and untradeable
mcf_translation: Walk-forward: each quarter, for every symbol x bar size, compute in-sample expectancy of RSI-momentum and RSI-reversion rules; trade next quarter only symbol/interval pairs above a threshold; must count all symbol x interval x rule combos as configurations tried.

setup_name: Combined-predictor SPY market timing (incl. variance risk premium)
conditions: Forecast 6-month-ahead (or 1-month-ahead) S&P excess return by combining ~20 published predictors (dividend/price, P/E, CAPE, variance risk premium = VIX minus realised S&P volatility, etc.)
Map forecast to over/underweight of SPY
entry_trigger: Set SPY exposure proportional to the combined forecast at each rebalance
stated_edge: Many predictors are individually weak out of sample but combining them yields a forecast strong enough to trade; variance risk premium is strongest near a 3-month horizon
stated_stats: Backtest 2001-2015: about twice SPY's average return at half the volatility (~4x Sharpe) - backtest only
data_needed: VIX history, valuation ratios (dividend yield, earnings, CAPE)
mcf_translation: Daily bars give realised vol; need VIX series. Simple test: monthly SPY exposure = f(VIX - 21-day realised vol); higher premium -> higher exposure. Not an intraday setup but could act as a regime filter for intraday long bias.

firm_or_style: prop (Seven Points Capital), discretionary momentum + scalping
setup_name: Descending triangle short in a faded low-cap runner
time_of_day: after the initial run stalls; often midday onward
universe_filter: Low-cap 'trash' names that have run up several hundred percent and started making lower highs
conditions: Stock already up a few hundred percent
Momentum stalls: a lower high forms after a dip
Successive dips and lower highs form a descending triangle over a flat-ish support
entry_trigger: Three possible shorts: (1) inside the triangle near a lower high, (2) on the break of triangle support, (3) on a failed retest of the broken support from below
stop: Above the triangle's last lower high (fixed dollar risk per entry)
target_or_exit: Not specified; trade the breakdown leg
management: Size larger only when the setup is clean; take every valid instance to keep results consistent
stated_edge: Exhausted runners lose buyers; lower highs show supply, and support breaks trigger liquidation
data_needed: Float data; reliable short-locate availability; low-cap universe coverage in MCF
mcf_translation: Universe: stocks with close >= 3x price of 5 sessions ago (or intraday gain > 100%). On 5-min bars, detect >= 2 lower swing highs with roughly flat swing lows (tolerance 1-2%); short on 5-min close below the flat low; stop above last swing high; exit at close or at 2R.

setup_name: Join the trend on a pullback into support
instrument: US stocks (large caps with catalysts, e.g. INTC/AAPL on news)
universe_filter: Names in play with fresh news/catalyst; gappers; scanner on volume, range, volatility, float
conditions: Stock trending up on a catalyst
Pulls back into a support level (prior breakout level / high-volume node on volume profile)
Volume and tape show sellers drying up at support
entry_trigger: Buy at support with a tight stop, sizing up because risk is small
stop: Just below support (where the pattern is invalidated)
target_or_exit: Ride the trend; if green by end of day, hold as a swing per exit rules
management: Fixed dollar risk per trade; scale in/out across prices; best trades work immediately
stated_edge: Pullbacks within established trends at high-volume support offer low risk relative to continuation
stated_stats: Guest reports green every month for ~3 years trading ~15 setups and ~50M shares/month (overall, not per setup)
mcf_translation: Stocks with gap > 3% and rvol > 2; trend = price above VWAP and rising 20-EMA on 5-min; entry when price pulls back to VWAP or prior-day high/opening-range high and the 5-min bar closes back above it; stop below the pullback low; exit at close (or hold overnight if day closes green above VWAP).

setup_name: Range scalping ('market making') in liquid low-priced stocks
horizon: scalp (<5 min) to intraday (up to ~1 hour)
universe_filter: Price $5-20, at least ~10M shares/day, daily range ~20-50 cents (e.g. AMD at the time)
conditions: Deep liquidity so size can be bought/sold without moving price
Stock oscillating within an intraday range
entry_trigger: Buy near the low end of the range / sell near the high end, posting or taking liquidity as needed
stop: Scratch quickly if price moves through the level
target_or_exit: Capture a piece of the intraday range
management: Trade size; relies on low/no commissions and rebates
stated_edge: Mean reversion inside the range plus near-zero execution costs at a prop firm
stated_stats: Share of firm P&L has declined vs momentum trading in recent years
data_needed: Tick/quote data; realistic per-share costs; MCF retail cost assumptions likely kill the edge
mcf_translation: Low priority: on 5-min bars for $5-20 stocks with ADV > 10M, fade touches of the morning range high/low back toward VWAP; must include full costs since the stated edge depends on near-zero fees.

firm_or_style: retail full-time day trader, long-biased small caps
setup_name: Intraday bull flag / pennant breakout in high-rvol sub-$10 stocks
time_of_day: from the open; first breakouts after an initial push
universe_filter: Price < $10; volume >= 2.5x average daily volume (Finviz scan); ranked A/B/C by chart, sector theme, low float, high short interest
conditions: Stock makes a strong move to a high of day
Pulls back / consolidates in a tight flag or pennant (3-min chart)
Price holding above VWAP
Daily and 1-hour charts not blocked by nearby resistance (check 20-day support/resistance, 50/200-day MAs)
entry_trigger: Buy the break above the consolidation high (never the first breakout of the day; wait for consolidation)
stop: Tight: just below the consolidation; exit fully at a scratch/small loss if the breakout fails
target_or_exit: Sell a first partial immediately into the breakout pop; scale out on the way up; final target at a daily level such as the 200-day MA; ~1/5 of size left by final target
management: Full size in one entry ('one bullet'), then take risk off right away; scale out if volume absorbs at a level without price progress
stated_edge: High relative volume means many participants watch the same levels; flags after a strong push break with follow-through; quick partials avoid failed-breakout losses
stated_stats: Reported ~1400% compounded return in 2017 with small drawdowns; one red day in the early part of the next year (self-reported, bull/crypto-mania period)
data_needed: Float and short interest optional; 3-min bars (MCF has 5-min)
mcf_translation: Universe: price < $10, rvol >= 2.5 by 10:00. On 5-min bars after a >= 5% push from open, detect 3-6 bar consolidation with range < 40% of the push and lows above VWAP; buy on break of consolidation high; stop below consolidation low; sell 1/3 at +1R, 1/3 at +2R, rest at close or VWAP loss.

setup_name: Hot-sector leader long when peers turn green
instrument: US stocks (theme/sector momentum names, e.g. blockchain names in Dec 2017)
universe_filter: 4-5 stocks in a speculative theme moving 50-100% daily; trade the leaders, not laggards
conditions: Theme is in a risk-on mania with heavy volume
Names open weak / red
One or two peers turn green on the day
entry_trigger: Buy the sector leader as peers flip green, using peers as leading indicators
stop: Below intraday low / VWAP (not specified exactly)
target_or_exit: Hold longer than a normal scalp while the theme is hot; stop pressing when friends/family start asking about the theme (crowding)
management: Bigger size while liquidity is deep; back off as the move gets extended
stated_edge: Correlated theme names move together; leaders outperform laggards
stated_stats: December 2017 was the guest's best month (more than first 5 months combined)
data_needed: Theme/sector groupings for small caps; news/catalyst tags
mcf_translation: Define groups (by sector code or user list). When >= 2 of group members cross from red to green vs prior close after opening down, buy the group member with the highest 5-day return on its own cross of prior close; stop below day low; exit at close.

firm_or_style: independent full-time short seller of small caps
setup_name: Backside short of a parabolic low-float hype runner
instrument: US stocks (low float, often < 5M shares, low priced)
time_of_day: any; often after day 3 of a parabolic run
universe_filter: Low-float stocks up several hundred to 1000%+ over days/weeks on news that does not justify the move (hype/manipulation; e.g. crypto/blockchain or MoviePass-type pivots); need short locates
conditions: Multi-day or multi-week run (the bigger the run, the higher the conviction)
Run is parabolic; often day 3+ of the parabolic leg
Exhaustion: big drop on heavy volume and/or failed bounce below a prior high (the 'backside')
entry_trigger: Starter short (e.g. 5-10k shares) at a failed bounce / breakdown; add only as it moves in your favour (hit the bid on breakdowns); never add to a losing short
stop: Above intraday resistance / high of day; exit if it breaks resistance, especially on volume ('paper cut' losses), then look to re-enter later
target_or_exit: Hold for the 40-70% collapse typical after the peak; may hold overnight or for weeks once on the backside
management: Small size on the front side; full/large size only on backside of multi-week runners; hold little overnight on day-1 runners due to PR/halt risk; several brokers for locates and fees
stated_edge: Hype runners on thin floats nearly always deflate; the 'air' in the price makes risk/reward on the backside very favourable
stated_stats: Guest says these few 'golden' setups (3-6 per year) produce ~75-80% of annual income; claims ~90-95% success on top setups (self-assessed)
data_needed: Float, short borrow availability and fees, halt data; low-cap coverage
mcf_translation: Universe: close >= 3x the close 10 sessions earlier and price > $2. Daily: after first day closing below prior day's low on volume >= 1.5x 10-day avg, short next open; stop above the run's high; exit after N days or at 50% retrace of the run. Intraday variant: on 5-min, short first lower high after a high-volume break of VWAP on a day-3+ runner; stop above HOD; cover at close. Add borrow fees to costs.

firm_or_style: ex-prop (TMG) fixed-income relative value, launching a CTA
setup_name: Treasury cash vs futures relative-value spread
instrument: US Treasury cash notes vs CME Treasury futures
universe_filter: On-the-run 5-30 year Treasuries and matching futures
conditions: Spread between cash bond and future deviates from its historical relationship given the rate regime (curve steepening/flattening)
entry_trigger: Long the cheap leg / short the rich leg when the model says over- or under-valued; execution is automated
stop: Pre-set risk parameters per contract volatility
management: Size cut when risk at the planned entry is too large; trade less in erratic regimes
stated_edge: Historical relationships between related rate instruments tend to persist; discretion on regime plus systematic execution
data_needed: Treasury cash and futures prices, carry/repo data
mcf_translation: Not mappable to MCF stock lab; conceptually similar to ETF pair spreads (e.g. IEF vs TLT) on daily bars.

setup_name: Bear-market rule: sell rallies, never sell big down days
universe_filter: Index in a confirmed bear regime (example: Nasdaq holds below a key level for about a month)
conditions: Bear regime confirmed
Market has a sharp rally / pop up toward resistance
entry_trigger: Short into the rally (or buy puts on the pop); on big down days buy near-the-money calls and short ~1.5 futures per call for defined-risk short exposure
management: Never initiate shorts after a large down day, to avoid 50-70 point short-covering rips
stated_edge: Bear markets do not fall in a straight line; violent rallies punish shorts added after big declines
mcf_translation: Daily SPY/QQQ: regime = close below 200-day MA for 20+ sessions. Short only after a 2-day rally of >= 2% (or close above 10-day MA), exit after N days or on new low; compare to shorting after down days >= 2%. Could serve as a direction/timing filter for intraday short setups in bear regimes.
